A new helper regenerates stored inline uuids that collide with the saved metrics attached by a saved_metrics_ids-only update. The docs also stop recommending the promote-then-attach flow. But upstream also changed _sync_ordering_with_metric_changes so the saved metric's uuid is not removed from the ordering when the inline copy gets a new uuid. The agent skipped this. In the already-linked scenarios the shared metric can vanish from the ordering, so the fix is incomplete.

The agent made the same core fixes in the same places. The saved-metric service now always mints a fresh uuid on create, which is identical to upstream. The experiment update now regenerates stored inline uuids that collide with the shared metrics being attached, so an update that only changes saved_metrics_ids no longer leaves a clash. It reaches this by a different route than upstream. The agent guidance no longer recommends the promote-then-attach flow. The agent skipped upstream's ordering-sync tweak, which only matters in an edge case where a collision already exists and the shared metric is already linked. The main behavior still matches.

The saved-metric service change matches upstream: a new shared metric always gets a fresh uuid. The docs were updated to stop recommending promote-then-attach. The agent also added a helper that regenerates a colliding stored inline uuid when an update changes only saved_metrics_ids, which is the right direction. But it omits the upstream ordering fix. Once the inline copy gets a new uuid, the old uuid belongs to the shared metric and must stay in the ordering arrays. The agent's helper runs after the normal dedup, so it likely drops that uuid from ordering, which makes the change partly incomplete.

results.evidence: In `normalize_query_for_write`, the old `elif not incoming_uuid:` is replaced by an unconditional `else:` branch: `normalized_query["uuid"] = str(uuid4())` whenever `existing_uuid` is falsy, so a supplied uuid is discarded on create. The rest is copied unchanged via `normalized_query = dict(query)` and stored with `query=normalized_query`.

`update_saved_metric` passes `existing_uuid = saved_metric.query.get("uuid")` into `normalize_query_for_write(update_data["query"], existing_uuid=existing_uuid)`, which does `if existing_uuid: normalized_query["uuid"] = existing_uuid`. A mismatching incoming uuid still raises "Saved metric UUID cannot be changed".

`_dedupe_stored_metrics_against_saved` loops `for field in ("metrics", "metrics_secondary")`, skips fields present in the payload, reads `stored_metrics = getattr(experiment, field, None) or []`, and on a clash (`metric.get("uuid") in attached_saved_metric_uuids`) sets `update_data[field] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(stored_metrics, seen=seen)` with `seen` containing the attached saved uuids. `_assign_uuids_to_metrics` regenerates any uuid `in seen`. It is called in the update path with `attached_saved_metric_uuids = self._collect_saved_metric_uuids(update_data["saved_metrics_ids"])`.

When no stored inline uuid matches, the helper hits `if not any(... metric.get("uuid") in attached_saved_metric_uuids ...): continue`, so `update_data[field]` is never set. The inline list is not pulled into the update, so neither the stored metrics nor any ordering sync driven by inline changes is touched.

The patch only rewrites the inline list (`update_data[field] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(...)`) and does not touch ordering logic. Whether the original uuid stays in the ordering depends on `_sync_ordering_with_metric_changes` and `_sync_ordering_for_saved_metrics_on_update`, neither of which is shown. The existing comment says regenerated uuids are appended "as additions", but if the inline sync treats the old uuid as removed from the inline list (old set minus new set), it would drop the original from the ordering; whether the saved-metric sync then re-adds it cannot be determined from the code provided.

`_dedupe_stored_metrics_against_saved` only writes `update_data["metrics"]` / `update_data["metrics_secondary"]`; it never modifies `saved_metrics_ids` or any `ExperimentSavedMetric`. Afterwards `saved_metrics_data: list[dict] = update_data.pop("saved_metrics_ids", []) or []` is taken unchanged from the request. `_collect_saved_metric_uuids` is read-only (`.only("query")`).

The revised guidance still says: "call `experiment-saved-metrics-create` with the same `query` (the `ExperimentMetric` object)" and never instructs omitting the `uuid` when creating the shared metric. It does add the removal part ("send the `saved_metrics_ids` attach and a `metrics` array without the inline copy in one `experiment-update` call"), but the instruction to omit the identifier is absent from both metric-configuration.md.j2 and SKILL.md.

The fresh-identifier half is provided: when `saved_metrics_ids` is absent, already-linked saved uuids are added to `seen_metric_uuids` (`for link in experiment.experimenttosavedmetric_set...: seen_metric_uuids.add(uuid)`) and `update_data["metrics"] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(update_data["metrics"], seen=seen_metric_uuids)` regenerates the clashing inline uuid. Whether the clashing uuid remains in the ordering depends on `_sync_ordering_with_metric_changes`, which is not shown and not changed by the patch; if it removes uuids no longer present in the inline list, the shared metric's entry would be dropped with nothing to re-add it, since the link already exists.
normalize_query_for_write now: `if existing_uuid: ... else: normalized_query["uuid"] = str(uuid4())` — incoming uuid discarded on create; rest of dict copied unchanged via dict(query).
`if existing_uuid: normalized_query["uuid"] = existing_uuid`; update_saved_metric passes existing_uuid from saved_metric.query.

_dedupe_stored_metrics_against_saved loops over ("metrics","metrics_secondary"), skips fields in update_data, and if a stored metric's uuid is in attached_saved_metric_uuids, sets update_data[field] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(stored_metrics, seen=seen) with seen containing the attached uuids, so clashing ones get new uuids.
`if not any(... in attached_saved_metric_uuids ...): continue` — no update_data entry is added when there's no clash, so stored metrics are untouched; ordering is not touched by this function.

The helper only puts new metric lists into update_data; ordering is handled by the existing _sync_ordering_with_metric_changes, which is not shown. The comment says it appends new uuids, and the original stays because the saved metric's uuid is in the ordering via _sync_ordering_for_saved_metrics_on_update, but whether the original is preserved rather than removed as a stale entry can't be confirmed from what is shown.
The helper only modifies update_data for metrics/metrics_secondary; saved_metrics_ids is popped and processed unchanged afterward, and the saved metric's query uuid is never rewritten.

The guidance in metric-configuration.md.j2 was rewritten to "Do not attach the new shared metric to the experiment the inline metric is still on... send the `saved_metrics_ids` attach and a `metrics` array without the inline copy in one `experiment-update` call." Because the creation service now mints a fresh uuid, the omit-identifier instruction is arguably implied, but the text never explicitly says to omit the identifier when creating the shared metric.

The existing path with seen_metric_uuids including attached_saved_metric_uuids (or the current links' uuids) feeds _assign_uuids_to_metrics on resent lists, regenerating clashing inline uuids; the original stays with the saved metric and, per the comments, in the ordering.

+        """Regenerate stored inline uuids that collide with the saved metrics this update attaches.

+        An update that only changes ``saved_metrics_ids`` never passes the stored inline lists
+        through dedup, so a saved metric can land on the experiment holding the uuid of an inline
